property_summary: For every caller, after a successful airDrop the caller's tokenBalance increases by exactly 20 (non-decreasing and specifically +20); removing the require guarding against non-decreasing behavior allows cases where the post-call balance does not equal previous+20 (the mutant can change reachable balances), so the mutant can violate this invariant for some inputs.

For every caller address, calling airDrop when they have zero balance and from an address that reports supportsToken() returns true will always increase that caller's tokenBalance by exactly 20 in the reference; the mutant (which removes the non-decreasing guard) allows reachable states where the post-call tokenBalance is not equal to pre+20 for some inputs.

For any caller who has zero prior tokenBalance and whose msg.sender externally advertises support for the token, a successful call to airDrop always results in that caller's tokenBalance being exactly previous_balance + 20; the mutant that removes the non-decreasing require can produce a case where the post-call balance is not equal to previous+20.

For every caller address that starts with nonzero storage at some other slot key (i.e., some address k with tokenBalance[k] != 0), calling airDrop from that caller in the reference never decreases any other account's tokenBalance (all tokenBalance[x] after the call are >= before); the mutant removing the non-decreasing guard can make some other key's balance decrease for some inputs.

For every caller address that satisfies hasNoBalance and whose msg.sender (the caller) advertises supportsToken(), a successful airDrop call on the reference contract leaves every account's tokenBalance unchanged except that the caller's balance increases by exactly 20; the mutant (removing the non-decreasing require) allows some other account's tokenBalance to change (decrease) for some inputs.

For every caller addr A and adversarial callee attacker, after airDrop(A) completes the total tokenBalance for any address K cannot change due to reentrancy in the correct contract (because _locked is set true during the call); the mutant that omits setting _locked = true allows a re-entrant attacker to change tokenBalance of some key K, so there exists inputs (caller and attacker) that make balances differ.
